title: Deferred Reference Replayer and Evolving Baseline CI Hook
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduce deferred reference replay runner and a CI hook that assesses reference drift against an evolving baseline. Adds observability metrics and an opt-in backfill trigger for reference resynthesis.

description: Summary: Adds a deferred reference replay runner and a CI hook that evaluates incoming PR-induced changes against an evolving baseline of reference outputs. Motivation: prompt-set regressions can occur not only because model behavior changes but because our canonical references become stale. Current CI gates assume a fixed gold baseline; this PR introduces a controlled way to resynthesize and compare references without creating noisy backfill churn. What this implements: 1) replay_runner.py: a new component that can (a) replay a PR's prompts against a pinned model snapshot, (b) optionally resynthesize a candidate reference using a configured synthesis policy, and (c) compute semantic_consistency_score between old and new references using embeddings + pairwise reranking. The runner supports a deferred mode where heavy synthesis is queued and executed after fast checks pass. 2) semantic_reranker.py: a lightweight embedding-based pairwise reranker + similarity normalizer to produce a per-example divergence score. 3) reference_replay_hook.py: a CI hook that runs as part of the eval stage. The hook performs a quick token-level smoke check; if the smoke check flags potential regressions, it enqueues a deferred replay job (deferred to a worker pool) which performs deeper semantic checks and emits metrics. 4) metrics and alerts: reference_metrics.py adds metrics: eval.reference_divergence (gauge), eval.replay_duration_ms (histogram), eval.resynthesis_count (counter). An alert (reference_divergence.alert) is added to trigger a backfill candidate only after sustained divergence across windows. 5) configs and opt-in: configs/defaults.yaml adds flags to control reranker.enabled (default false), replay.max_samples_per_pr (default 2000), and replay.backfill_threshold. 6) docs: docs/eval/replay_and_baseline.md describes operational workflow and guidance for teams. Tests: test_replay_runner.py covers deterministic replay for pinned models, snapshot locking, and semantic scoring edge cases. Performance: added bench_replay_latency.yml to capture latency and resource usage for the reranker; we measured median overhead of ~90-140ms per sample when reranker is enabled, which is why reranker is opt-in. Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag - Enable CI hook in canary projects (internal teams) for 2 weeks - Observe eval.reference_divergence and replay_duration metrics - If steady, enable reranker for broader org and allow opt-in backfills via an internal request ticket. Backfill policy: the CI hook will never automatically rewrite canonical references. Instead, it creates a backfill candidate with a justification payload; a manual or automated policy (separate operator flow) approves and schedules the resynthesis/backfill. This is to avoid accidental corruption of gold sets. Related work: follows work on cohort-based gating (ENG-4312) and prompt-order robustness (ENG-3999). Tests and CI: updated pipeline.yml to include deferred job orchestration; added a Dockerfile for the worker image. CI status: all unit tests and integration smoke runs passed in the final run; one earlier run failed due to a race on snapshot writes which was fixed by adding an explicit file-level lock. Review summary: reviewers requested configuration toggles, perf guidance, and an alert dampening strategy; all comments addressed. Merge: squashed and merged to main (merge method: squash). Why this is different: instead of a binary pass/fail gate, this PR introduces a tiered approach (fast token checks, deferred semantic checks, operator-reviewed backfill candidates) that reduces noise while surfacing real reference drift that can cause latent regressions. Operational note: teams that want aggressive automatic backfills should enable replay.backfill_policy=auto in a separate opt-in configuration and accept the risk.
